findings.evidence: Verify: run the verification gates for the components you touched (the check, lint and test commands named in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or the Makefile ...), plus one acceptance check ... use the toolchain's standard test runner
findings.fix: Shorten step 5 to the non-obvious parts: the cross-component acceptance check, the changed-validator self-test and 'no gate found → mark unverified'. Drop the generic list of where test commands live, because the model already looks for them there. Do the same for 'reproduce a bug before fixing' in step 2 (line 13).

findings.evidence: Plan: before any edit, record per requirement its owner, dependency order and acceptance check; subtasks sharing files stay in one worker.
findings.fix: Add a checkpoint after planning (plan-validate-execute): 'Before delegating, check the plan: every requirement has exactly one owner, no two parallel workers share a file, and every acceptance check is a command you can run. Revise until all three hold.' This turns the plan into a validated artifact rather than just a note.

findings.evidence: They may run in another checkout.
findings.fix: Give this gotcha its corrective action where it is stated: 'They may run in another checkout: pass the absolute worktree path and require them to report `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and HEAD.' Then the NEVER item on line 34 becomes the consequence, not the only remedy.

name: multi-component-coordinator (rename the file to match). The current name clashes with the built-in `general-purpose` agent. Whether a plugin agent overrides that built-in is UNVERIFIED in docs/audit/artifact-specs.md, and plugin agents have the lowest priority, so an unscoped `general-purpose` dispatch may resolve to the built-in and never reach this agent.

findings.evidence: else re-delegate to the owning worker with the conflicting signatures, then repeat this diff.
findings.fix: Bound the integration loop the same way step 6 bounds gate failures: 'at most 3 integrate-diff rounds; then list the remaining signature mismatches under Remaining blockers and mark the work incomplete.' As written, a worker that keeps returning mismatched signatures loops forever.

findings.evidence: Done only when every requested acceptance criterion is met and required validation succeeds.
findings.fix: Resolve the conflict with step 2's pre-existing failures: 'Required validation succeeds when no test fails that was not listed as pre-existing in the step 2 baseline.' Otherwise a worktree that already has failing tests can never reach done.

findings.evidence: "Parallel workers committing in one checkout race on the git index: serialize commits, or give each worker its own paths and have it commit only those (`git commit -- <paths>`)." The second branch does not eliminate concurrency conflicts: disjoint-path commits still share the index, HEAD and their locks.
findings.fix: Replace this instruction with: Parallel workers share one index and HEAD even when editing disjoint files. Serialize commits and other index/HEAD mutations in a shared checkout. Use `git commit -- <paths>` only to constrain commit contents, not as an alternative to serialization; parallel commits require isolated worktrees.
